device.name: WeatherFlow Tempest Weather Station
device.notes:
The WeatherFlow Tempest (and the legacy Air/Sky sensors) is a home weather station whose hub broadcasts JSON observation datagrams on the LAN — no cloud needed to receive them and no authentication. WeatherFlow publishes the local UDP API itself.
TRANSPORT: JSON over UDP broadcast, port 50222. Passive: a client just listens; every message carries hub/device serial numbers.
MESSAGE TYPES:
  rapid_wind   ~3 s wind speed (m/s) + direction (deg)
  obs_st       the Tempest combined observation (see fields below)
  obs_air / obs_sky   legacy Air / Sky sensor observations
  evt_precip   rain start;  evt_strike   lightning (distance km, energy)
  device_status  per-device health (bit-flag sensor status)
  hub_status     firmware revision, uptime, RSSI
obs_st observation array (order): wind lull/avg/gust (m/s), wind direction (deg), station pressure (mb), air temperature (C), relative humidity (%), illuminance (lux), UV index, solar radiation (W/m^2), rain accumulation (mm), lightning strike distance/count, battery volts, report interval.

openness.notes: This is the vendor's own local broadcast API, published deliberately for third-party clients (weewx, Home Assistant). Nothing here was reverse-engineered.

upstream_docs.covers: The UDP port, message types and the obs_st / rapid_wind / evt_* field layouts.
upstream_docs.title: WeatherFlow — Tempest UDP API v171

credentials.notes: The local UDP broadcast is unauthenticated and read-only; the Wi-Fi passphrase is handled by the app's onboarding, not the API documented here.

factory_reset.description: Two different pieces of hardware with two different buttons, and it is worth being clear which one is being reset: the hub is the thing that holds the WiFi credentials and emits the UDP broadcasts this spec documents, while the sensors only talk to the hub. A sensor whose observations have stopped appearing needs the sensor procedure; a hub that needs to move to a new network needs the first one.
factory_reset.effect: On the hub, clears the saved WiFi connection and returns it to onboarding. On a Tempest or SKY sensor, drops its association with the hub and puts it back into pairing mode. Neither clears the observation history, which lives in the vendor's cloud rather than on the hardware.

procedures.name: Hub: clear the saved WiFi connection

steps.action: With the hub powered, press and hold the reset button on the back using a toothpick or a straightened clip.

steps.expect: The saved WiFi connection is cleared and the hub returns to onboarding.

procedures.basis: WeatherFlow's Tempest instruction manual, listed under sensors not reporting.
procedures.indicator: The blue LED on the back of the hub.
procedures.name: Hub: radio reset, held while power is applied

steps.action: Using a thin tool, press and hold the reset button on the back.
Reconnect power while still holding the button.
Wait for the blue LED on the back, then release.
steps.expect: Blue LED on the back of the hub.

procedures.name: Tempest or SKY sensor: back to pairing mode

steps.action: Press and hold the clear LED button on the base of the unit, next to the battery door, for about five seconds.
steps.notes: On a SKY with the solar panel accessory fitted, reach the same button with a thin tool through the slot in the panel rather than removing it.

steps.action: Release when the LED flashes green.
steps.expect: LED flashes green — the device is in pairing mode and can be re-added to the station.

methods.description: Onboard the hub onto Wi-Fi with the WeatherFlow app. After it joins the LAN it broadcasts observations on UDP 50222 with no further setup.

steps.action: Onboard the hub onto Wi-Fi with the WeatherFlow app.
steps.expect: The hub broadcasts obs_st / rapid_wind datagrams on UDP 50222.

setup.notes: The hub's Wi-Fi onboarding is app-driven (not part of the local UDP API); once the hub is on the LAN it broadcasts with no further setup and no account needed for local reads.

rejoin.notes: Wi-Fi is reconfigured through the app; local broadcasts resume once the hub rejoins.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The UDP port, message types and obs_st field order are from WeatherFlow's own published UDP API (v171).
